project.name: ESP32 Weather Station → AWS IoT → Timestream → Dashboard
project.description: ESP32 weather station publishes readings through AWS IoT Core MQTT/TLS; an IoT Rule invokes a prediction Lambda; readings/forecasts are stored in a backend database and served by a second Lambda through API Gateway to a browser dashboard.
project.implementation_status: Not independently verified; documentation describes deployment instructions rather than proof of a successful live deployment.

common_flow: Connects via 2.4 GHz phone hotspot or Wi-Fi
Publishes JSON over MQTT/TLS to AWS IoT Core topic weather/data
IoT Rule weather_to_lambda invokes prediction Lambda
Prediction Lambda computes a 10-hour forecast and persists readings/forecasts
API Gateway GET /weather invokes weather-api Lambda
Dashboard fetches JSON and refreshes every 60 seconds

storage_variants.quick_setup: DynamoDB table weather-readings with device_id (String) partition key and timestamp (String) sort key.
storage_variants.original_documentation: Amazon Timestream database weatherdb, table readings, 12-hour memory retention.

known_document_conflicts: Document title and original deployment describe Timestream, but top diagram and REAL PROJECT SETUP describe DynamoDB.
Quick setup instructs DynamoDBFullAccess while prediction Lambda environment variables TS_DATABASE and TS_TABLE are Timestream-specific.
Lambda function names are case-sensitive (Weather-predict vs weather-predict).
API route depends on stage: /prod/weather vs /weather.
Firmware file table says DHT22 but hardware and wiring instructions specify BME280.
Original docs mention a touch switch and 1.8-inch ST7735 TFT; quick setup omits touch-switch wiring.

hardware.connectivity: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi hotspot; 5 GHz-only hotspot is incompatible.

firmware.security_note: Never commit secrets.h, private keys, or certificates.

api_lambda.name: weather-api
api_lambda.task: Read stored weather information and return JSON

security_notes: Prefer least-privilege IAM policies over broad AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess
Never place private keys in the dashboard or public repository
Review public API/CORS settings before production deployment

forecast_model.type: Physics-based heuristic, no training data required
forecast_model.humidity: Approximate inverse change of -2.5 percentage points RH per +1°C temperature
forecast_model.rain_likelihood: Heuristic based on high relative humidity and small temperature–dew-point spread
limitations: Heuristic projection, not a trained meteorological model
Rain likelihood is not a calibrated probability
Validate against observed data before accuracy claims.

troubleshooting.mqtt_rc_minus_2: Check IoT endpoint and device certificate/private key
troubleshooting.mqtt_drops: Verify IoT policy client ID matches THING_NAME
troubleshooting.bme280_missing: Verify I2C wiring and address 0x76 or 0x77
troubleshooting.tft_black: Verify TFT_eSPI driver/setup and SPI GPIO mapping
troubleshooting.lambda_access_denied: Check IAM policies and propagation; retry after delay
troubleshooting.api_empty_array: Publish a reading, check query window and storage pipeline
troubleshooting.cors_error: Verify HTTP API CORS and Lambda response headers

cost_notes.document_estimate: At one message per minute, roughly 43,000 MQTT messages/month and roughly 86,000 Lambda invocations/month.
cost_notes.caution: Free-tier limits, Timestream and API Gateway charges change; check current AWS pricing.

project.name: DocuChat
project.description: Next.js PDF chat application (RAG): upload PDFs, ask questions, and receive answers with citations retrieved via vector similarity search.
project.architecture: Next.js 14 (Pages Router), React 18, Prisma, PostgreSQL with pgvector, NextAuth.js, OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims), Anthropic Claude, Tailwind CSS.

documented_data_flow: Validate PDF type and the 5 MB max size on both client and server.
Store uploaded bytes in the database while processing is pending.
Parse PDF text asynchronously; handle corrupt or password-protected files gracefully.
Split text into semantically meaningful chunks with overlap and paragraph awareness.
Store embeddings in PostgreSQL via pgvector.
At question time, embed the query, run vector similarity search, retrieve relevant chunks.
Send question plus retrieved context to Anthropic Claude.
Return an answer with citations to source chunks and explicit truncation warnings.

setup_commands.pgvector: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f sql/enable-pgvector.sql (enables vector extension, adds embedding vector(1536) column because Prisma cannot create Unsupported columns, creates similarity-search index)

project_structure.lib/: Core logic: chunking, embeddings, vector search, Claude integration

credentials: Never hardcode API keys in source.
uploads: Handle corrupt and password-protected PDFs gracefully.
rate_limiting: Current in-memory limiter is not shared across instances.
Use Redis-backed limiter (e.g. Upstash) for multi-instance deployments.
storage_scaling: Database bytea storage only until processing completes.
For large scale, consider object storage such as S3 or Cloudflare R2.
authorization: Full document ownership model not documented — verify users can only access their own documents/chunks.
deployment_readiness: 'Production-grade' is the documentation's claim; no code, tests, audit or benchmark were supplied.
Verify migrations, error handling, observability, authorization, and provider failure behavior against the actual repository.

working_rules: Read the actual repository before changing code.
Preserve the Next.js 14 Pages Router architecture unless asked to migrate.
Keep the stack: React 18, Prisma, PostgreSQL+pgvector, NextAuth, OpenAI embeddings, Anthropic Claude, Tailwind.
Keep embedding dimension consistent at 1536 (text-embedding-3-small, vector(1536)).
Maintain client- and server-side PDF validation with a 5 MB maximum.
Preserve async PDF processing and clear errors for corrupt/password-protected PDFs.
Use paragraph-aware chunking with overlap; do not invent numeric chunk settings without checking the code.
Ground RAG answers in retrieved passages with citations; surface truncation warnings.
Never expose API keys or secrets in client bundles, logs, or commits.
Do not assume in-memory rate limiting is adequate for multiple instances.
Do not assume document-level authorization exists until verified.
Run tests and build checks after changes, and report what was actually run.

Never claim untested code is tested.
